questions.text: Can the radiologist clarify which description of the MRI is accurate?

name: General Medicine
routing_reason: Broad view of the whole case.

confidence.reason: The key investigation is described in two conflicting ways.

findings.statement: Routine blood tests are within the reference ranges.
The difference between the two documents may be a wording or copying difference in one of them, but this cannot be told from the documents alone.

uncertainties.text: Which document correctly describes the scan is unknown.

missing_info.why_it_matters: It is the only way to settle which description is accurate.

contradictions.description: The MRI report and the discharge summary describe the same scan differently.

questions.text: Can a formal re-read of the MRI be arranged?
Is the 3-month follow-up MRI still needed if the original report is confirmed?

evidence_refs.title: Sample summary: when an imaging report and a clinical summary disagree
Sample summary: recurrent headaches with brief visual symptoms

name: Neurology
routing_reason: Recurrent headaches and an MRI discrepancy.

findings.statement: The MRI report impression states no intracranial abnormality.
The discharge summary describes a small lesion in the right frontal lobe on the same scan.
When two documents describe a scan differently, a formal re-read by the reporting radiologist is commonly requested before conclusions are drawn.
Headaches preceded by short-lasting visual symptoms are a pattern in which migraine with aura is commonly considered.

uncertainties.text: Until the discrepancy is resolved, it is not possible to say whether the scan shows anything that needs follow-up.

considerations.statement: The planned follow-up MRI in 3 months is consistent with the discharge summary's description. Whether it is still needed depends on the clarification.

limitations: The MRI images were not available, only the reports.

questions.text: Could my frequent ibuprofen use be affecting my headaches?

evidence_refs.title: Sample summary: frequent painkiller use and headaches

findings.statement: Ibuprofen is used on about 15 days a month, alongside sumatriptan when needed.
Using painkillers on many days each month is associated with more frequent headaches in some people. This is worth reviewing with the prescriber.
